claims.text: The recorded distances settle the deviation: the platform records 17.6 km actually driven against a 16.2 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.40 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. The case therefore cannot fall in the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix, and a refund row is live.

The route actually taken is not in dispute and the trace that shows it is clean: the driver-device trace carries 57 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s and a map-matched road on every fix, and it puts the vehicle on the Central Expressway to 10:48:41 and on Upper Thomson Road from 10:49:11, matching the recorded deviation at 10:49:23 and the rejoin at Balestier Road / Thomson Road at 11:03:14. POL-RD-22 makes the trace the record of which route was taken and when.

POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data intersects the recommended route, and the only advisory on file does not establish that intersection. The HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory is on the Central Expressway towards the City at 'after Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1 exit to PIE' and overlaps the trip window, but its own derived fields leave intersects_route and justifies_reroute null, and the derivation states in terms that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The intersection limb of POL-RD-23 is therefore not made out on this record.

The driver's own words are not traffic data. His chat message 'Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?' is a party's assertion, and POL-RD-23 provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The chat artifact EV-CHAT-06012 is impaired at weight 0.9 on issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH, and I disclose that; it is cited here only for the text of that message, which is what the driver said, not for any fact the impairment touches.

Because the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation is over 1 km, row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full: the deviation distance times the per-km rate, 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD, which the fare breakdown computes as 1.01 SGD. The rider filed this dispute, so PARTIAL_REFUND returns that sum to the rider; the rider presses for the matrix's own measure of the excess, 1.01 SGD, and not the 4.80 SGD headline, because the matrix is the remedy the policy provides and the rider asks for nothing the policy does not give.

Rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both refund the excess distance fare; the only row that leaves the rider carrying the whole charge is row (a), which needs a traffic-justified reroute that the rider was informed of and agreed to. The rider does not dispute the chat: the driver asked at 10:46:33 and the rider answered 'Ok can, thanks' at 10:47:03, before the point of deviation, which would satisfy POL-RD-21's agreement limb. But that acknowledgment is carried solely by EV-CHAT-06012, which is impaired at weight 0.9 on SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH, so POL-GEN-02(2) caps any finding that turns on it at 0.9, while the driver's profile carries fraud_flags of 2, which under POL-GEN-22 lifts the confidence required for an AI ruling to 0.95. A row (a) NO_ACTION that leaves the rider paying the excess cannot be entered at the confidence the policy demands, and the case must be resolved on a row that does not depend on the impaired chat.

If the Judge is not persuaded that the advisory fails the intersection limb, but is also unable to find from the record that it meets it, then the traffic-justification fact POL-RD-23 needs cannot be established on this evidence, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation with the open question stated rather than an outcome inferred from the gap. POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-03 carry ESCALATE for this category, and on an escalation no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than collected, so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge.

claims.text: The deviation is established as 1.40 km, and it is over the tolerance: POL-RD-22 measures deviation as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km, the platform's recorded distances, and this record carries 17.60 km actual against 16.20 km recommended. That is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, which puts the case in the 'over 1 km' limb of the POL-RD-24 matrix. The trip record is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance (POL-RD-22).

POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of a deviation by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. The chat shows exactly that: the driver wrote at 10:46:33 'Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?' - a brief reason, which the clause says is enough - and the rider answered at 10:47:03 'Ok can, thanks'. DISCLOSURE under POL-GEN-02(1): the chat artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.9; the issue code that fired is SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH (severity LOW), a version tag on an export that is not truncated and whose four messages map one-to-one, and it does not touch the acknowledgement recorded.

The notice came before the point of deviation, not after it. The trip record's own event log places route_deviation_detected at 10:49:23 at the CTE / Yio Chu Kang Road exit, and the driver's message was sent at 10:46:33 - nearly three minutes earlier - and read by the rider at 10:47:23, before her reply. The driver's message timestamps are independently carried by the COMPLETE trip record's messages_during_trip block (MSG-06012-003 and MSG-06012-004), so this timing does not depend on the impaired chat export.

The reroute is traffic-justified on this record under POL-RD-23, which requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The LTA advisory LTA-TI-261003-6413 is typed HEAVY_TRAFFIC, a congestion class the policy's admissible-type map accepts as justifying a reroute, and it names the Central Expressway (CTE) towards City with a validity window of 10:16:11 to 11:26:11 that overlaps the trip (started 10:36:11, ended 11:04:11) and covers the deviation at 10:49:23. The CTE is a leg of the recommended route (Canberra Link, Seletar Expressway, Central Expressway, Balestier Road), and the driver's trace places the vehicle on the CTE from its first CTE fix at 10:45:11 until 10:48:41, so the advisory intersects the recommended route segment the driver was actually on.

Exactly one row of the POL-RD-24 matrix applies, and the evidence fills row (a): the reroute was traffic-justified (POL-RD-23), the rider was informed and agreed (POL-RD-21), and the deviation exceeded 1 km (POL-RD-22). Row (a) provides no refund. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and never means 'restore a charge': the rider filed, the fare of 21.41 SGD is CHARGED on the ledger and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the present state already reflects the correct outcome - the rider's claim is simply not supported.

Row (a) is not displaced by the matrix's escalation carve-out for a case that 'fits no row (for example, informed but the rider objected)'. There was no objection: the rider wrote 'Ok can, thanks' at 10:47:03, and her own filing records 'I said ok in the chat'. A fare complaint raised at 18:42:11, some eight hours after the trip ended at 11:04:11, is not an objection at the point of deviation, and it cannot retroactively un-agree a deviation the rider accepted in the chat while the vehicle was still on the road.

The 4.80 SGD the rider claims has no basis in the policy's arithmetic. POL-RD-24 fixes the only sum the matrix can return on this record at the excess distance fare - deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge - which is 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD, and that only on rows (b) and (d), neither of which applies here. The ledger confirms per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, total_charged 21.41 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the claimed figure is overstated several times over on the rider's own best case.

The notice and the acknowledgement do not stand or fall on the impaired chat export. The COMPLETE trip record, weight 1.0, independently lists MSG-06012-003 (driver, 10:46:33) and MSG-06012-004 (rider, 10:47:03) in its messages_during_trip block, and POL-GEN-02(2) takes the highest weight among independent artifacts carrying the deciding fact. The single impairment in this record - the chat log at 0.9 for SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH - therefore does not lower the weight of the agreed-deviation finding, and I name it rather than presenting it as clean.

This is a case the AI may finish on this record. The contested amount is 4.80 SGD, and the facts that decide it - the recorded distances, the message timestamps, the advisory window and its type - all rest on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, the only impairment being a 0.9 schema tag on the chat export. Whatever elevated confidence POL-GEN-22 requires where a profile carries fraud flags is met on this record, and POL-RD-25's condition on an AI ruling is satisfied, so no escalation is called for.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider (R-15817) and the driver (D-43200):

WHAT IS SETTLED. The deviation is not in doubt. The trip record EV-TRIP-06012 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records 17.6 km actually driven against a 16.2 km recommended route — 1.40 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 — and the GPS trace EV-GPS-06012 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) confirms which route was taken and when. This is an over-tolerance case, so the within-tolerance rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix are out.

WHY THE AI CANNOT FINISH IT. Two matters then decide the case, and neither can be carried to the confidence this dispute requires (POL-GEN-22 sets 0.95 because the driver's profile carries fraud_flags 2; POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-23's sibling rules send an under-confidence route-deviation case to a human).

(1) Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The only traffic data on file is the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-06012-01 — HEAVY_TRAFFIC (an admissible congestion class), on the Central Expressway towards the City, window 10:16–11:26, which covers the trip. The CTE is a leg of the recommended route (Canberra Link → SLE → CTE → Balestier Road) and the advisory is in the direction of travel, so on the better view it intersects the recommended route and the reroute is traffic-justified; I do not accept that it is affirmatively non-justified, and I therefore do not enter row (d). But the advisory's own derived record leaves 'intersects the recommended route' undetermined and states the record does not say whether it lies on the recommended route, so if that fact is treated as not established, POL-GEN-26 sends the case to a human on that open question. Either way the traffic limb is not something an AI ruling can close at 0.95.

(2) Informing and agreement (POL-RD-21; POL-RD-24 row (a)). If the reroute is traffic-justified, the only row that leaves the rider carrying the fare is row (a) — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, over 1 km, no refund. Row (b) is unavailable because the rider was informed. The informing and the agreement rest on the chat log EV-CHAT-06012, which is IMPAIRED: weight 0.9, issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence on any finding that turns on it is capped at 0.9, below the 0.95 POL-GEN-22 requires, so a row (a) NO_ACTION cannot be entered. The driver's argument that EV-TRIP-06012 independently carries the messages does not lift the cap: that block lists only the message ids, senders and timestamps (MSG-06012-003 at 10:46:33, MSG-06012-004 at 10:47:03), not their text, so the content of the informing and the agreement is carried by the 0.9 chat alone.

THE ARITHMETIC. The rider's 4.80 SGD headline has no basis in POL-RD-24 in any event. The excess distance fare the matrix can return is the deviation distance times the per-km rate: 1.40 × 0.72 = 1.01 SGD (EV-FARE-06012). That figure would be the refund only on row (b) or row (d), and I do not find row (d) made out; so no refund issues.

OUTCOME. The case is escalated. Both amounts are null and the 4.80 SGD in dispute is held, not collected or refunded. Open question for the human reviewer: whether the LTA advisory intersects the recommended route, and if it does, whether the rider's acknowledgment (chat log, weight 0.9, SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH) can be relied on at the 0.95 confidence the driver's fraud flags require.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute goes to a human reviewer (ESCALATE). No money moves now — the disputed SGD 4.80 is held, not refunded to the rider and not collected from the driver, and no compensation is payable.

What the record establishes. The platform's recorded distances (EV-TRIP-06012) give a deviation of 1.40 km — 17.6 km driven against a 16.2 km recommended route — above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, and the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-06012) shows which route was taken and when. At the ledger's SGD 0.72 per km (EV-FARE-06012) the excess-distance fare is SGD 1.01, not the SGD 4.80 claimed.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-06012-01) is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC — a congestion-class — advisory on the Central Expressway towards the City, valid 10:16 to 11:26, overlapping the trip (10:36 to 11:04) and covering the 10:49:23 deviation. The CTE is a leg of the recommended route (Canberra Link, SLE, CTE, Balestier Road), the advisory is in the direction of travel, and its position (after Ang Mo Kig Ave 1, towards the PIE) lies on the stretch the recommended route would have used south of where the driver left it. It therefore intersects the recommended route, and the reroute is traffic-justified. The rider is right that the driver's own chat assertion is not traffic data, but that is immaterial: the advisory, not the assertion, carries the justification.

Informing and agreement (POL-RD-21). The in-app chat (EV-CHAT-06012) shows the driver told the rider at 10:46:33 and the rider replied 'Ok can, thanks' at 10:47:03, both before the deviation at 10:49:23. The deviation was therefore agreed, and row (a) of the POL-RD-24 matrix — traffic-justified, informed and agreed, over 1 km — would give no refund. The rider's contrary arguments that the advisory fails the intersection limb and that row (d) refunds SGD 1.01 are rejected for the reason above.

Why the AI cannot finish it. The chat export is impaired at weight 0.9 (issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH), and the informing-and-agreement rests on it. The trip record's messages_during_trip block repeats the same message ids and times but not their text; it would not support the agreement with the chat removed, so it is not an independent carrier, and the confidence this ruling can carry is capped at 0.9 under POL-GEN-02(2). The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 2, so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 for an AI ruling, and POL-RD-25 escalates a route deviation where that is not met. No row of the POL-RD-24 matrix can be entered at 0.95: row (a) turns on the 0.9 chat, while rows (b) and (d) are contradicted by the record (the rider was informed; the reroute is traffic-justified).

Open question for the reviewer: whether the acknowledgment in the impaired chat export, on its own, supports the agreed-deviation finding at the confidence the fraud flag demands. Route deviation carries no referral clause in this version.

ruling.explanation:
To Rider R-15817 and Driver D-43200: the AI cannot finalise this one, so it goes to a human reviewer, and no money moves while it is held.

What is settled. The deviation is not in doubt. The platform's trip record EV-TRIP-06012 records 17.60 km driven against a 16.20 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.40 km (POL-RD-22). That is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the case sits in the over-1-km part of the POL-RD-24 matrix, and the rider's 4.80 SGD headline is not the matrix's measure: the excess distance fare is 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.01 SGD, not 4.80 (EV-FARE-06012).

The reroute is traffic-justified. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-06012-01 is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC (congestion-class) advisory on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards the City, valid 10:16-11:26, overlapping the trip (10:36-11:04). Its derived fields leave the route-intersection for the Judge, and on its road (the CTE, a leg of the recommended route) and its direction (city-bound, the direction of travel) it lies on the recommended route, so POL-RD-23 is satisfied. I therefore reject the rider's claim that the intersection limb is not made out: the null derived fields are a hook for the Judge's own reading of road, direction and window, not a missing fact.

On the merits this points to row (a): the driver informed the rider before deviating and the rider agreed. The chat EV-CHAT-06012 shows the driver's message at 10:46:33 ('Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?') and the rider's reply at 10:47:03 ('Ok can, thanks'), both before the deviation was detected at 10:49:23 (POL-RD-21). Row (a) would leave the rider carrying the charge.

Why the AI cannot enter that row. The only artifact that carries the content of those two messages is the chat log, and the pre-pass marks EV-CHAT-06012 IMPAIRED at weight 0.9 on issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH. The driver's argument that the COMPLETE trip record independently carries the notice and the acknowledgment is rejected: EV-TRIP-06012's messages_during_trip block lists only message ids, senders and timestamps, not the words exchanged, so it does not carry the agreed-deviation fact and cannot lift the cap. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence is capped at 0.9. Because the driver's profile carries fraud_flags of 2 (EV-DPROF-06012), POL-GEN-22 requires 0.95 for an AI ruling here, whatever the 4.80 SGD value. 0.9 falls below 0.95, so POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-22 require the case to go to a human reviewer. The rider's fallback that the case should instead be resolved on row (d) is also rejected: where the row that fits cannot be entered at the required confidence, the policy does not license substituting a different row.

For the human reviewer, the open question is whether the rider's acknowledgment in the chat is accepted at full weight and the traffic justification confirmed; that decides between row (a) (NO_ACTION, no refund) and any refund row, and the excess distance fare on the matrix is 1.01 SGD, not the 4.80 SGD claimed. The disputed sum is held, not collected or refunded. No clause of the route-deviation policy produces a referral here.

This dispute goes to a human reviewer. No refund and no compensation issue, and the 4.80 SGD contested is held rather than collected or returned.

The deviation is established. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-06012, weight 1.0) records 17.60 km driven against a recommended 16.20 km — 1.40 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 — and the clean driver-device trace (EV-GPS-06012, weight 1.0) shows the route taken (CTE until 10:48:41, then Upper Thomson Road and Thomson Road, rejoining at Balestier Road). The within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of the POL-RD-24 matrix are therefore out.

I reject the rider's argument that the LTA advisory fails POL-RD-23's intersection limb, and with it the rider's claim that row (d) applies. The advisory (EV-ADVIS-06012-01, weight 1.0) is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC (congestion-class) advisory on the Central Expressway towards the City; the CTE is a leg of the recommended route (Canberra Link, SLE, CTE, Balestier Road), and its window 10:16:11–11:26:11 overlaps the trip window 10:36:11–11:04:11. On its road, direction and location it lies on the recommended route, so the reroute is traffic-justified and the not-justified rows (d) and (e) are out. The rider's point that the driver's chat words are not traffic data is correct, but the justification rests on the LTA advisory, not on the driver's message.

That leaves rows (a) and (b), which turn on POL-RD-21's informed-and-agreed limb. The chat log (EV-CHAT-06012) shows the driver's message at 10:46:33 ('Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?') and the rider's 'Ok can, thanks' at 10:47:03, before the deviation at 10:49:23; on that record the deviation is agreed and row (a) — no refund — would apply. But that acknowledgement is carried only by EV-CHAT-06012, which is impaired: weight 0.9, issue code SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH. POL-GEN-02(2) caps any finding that rests on it at 0.9. The driver's profile carries fraud_flags of 2, so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 for an AI ruling. 0.9 is below 0.95, so under POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-22 the case cannot be finalised, and no row of the POL-RD-24 matrix can be entered at the confidence the policy demands (POL-GEN-26). I accept the rider's point that a row (a) holding cannot be entered at the required confidence; I do not accept the rider's conclusion that the case should then be decided on some other, chat-independent row — none applies. The rider's fallback escalation claim is right in substance, for this reason.

For the driver: the argument that the COMPLETE trip record (EV-TRIP-06012) independently carries the notice and acknowledgement at weight 1.0 does not hold. Its messages_during_trip block and the chat log are the same messages from the same source, not two independent carriers, and the block carries no message text, so POL-GEN-02(2)'s highest-weight rule does not engage. For the rider: the 4.80 SGD sought has no basis in any event — the most the matrix ever returns is the excess distance fare, 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD — but nothing issues now because the case is escalated.

Open question for the reviewer: whether the acknowledgement recorded in the impaired chat export (EV-CHAT-06012, weight 0.9, SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH) is enough to hold the rider to an agreed deviation, given that the driver's fraud_flags of 2 require a 0.95 confidence. Referrals: none — the route-deviation policy carries no referral clause.

ledger.claim: The recorded distances settle the deviation: the platform records 17.6 km actually driven against a 16.2 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.40 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. The case therefore cannot fall in the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix, and a refund row is live.

The route actually taken is not in dispute and the trace that shows it is clean: the driver-device trace carries 57 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s and a map-matched road on every fix, and it puts the vehicle on the Central Expressway to 10:48:41 and on Upper Thomson Road from 10:49:11, matching the recorded deviation at 10:49:23 and the rejoin at Balestier Road / Thomson Road at 11:03:14. POL-RD-22 makes the trace the record of which route was taken and when.

POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data intersects the recommended route, and the only advisory on file does not establish that intersection. The HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory is on the Central Expressway towards the City at 'after Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1 exit to PIE' and overlaps the trip window, but its own derived fields leave intersects_route and justifies_reroute null, and the derivation states in terms that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The intersection limb of POL-RD-23 is therefore not made out on this record.

The driver's own words are not traffic data. His chat message 'Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?' is a party's assertion, and POL-RD-23 provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The chat artifact EV-CHAT-06012 is impaired at weight 0.9 on issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH, and I disclose that; it is cited here only for the text of that message, which is what the driver said, not for any fact the impairment touches.

Because the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation is over 1 km, row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full: the deviation distance times the per-km rate, 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD, which the fare breakdown computes as 1.01 SGD. The rider filed this dispute, so PARTIAL_REFUND returns that sum to the rider; the rider presses for the matrix's own measure of the excess, 1.01 SGD, and not the 4.80 SGD headline, because the matrix is the remedy the policy provides and the rider asks for nothing the policy does not give.

Rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both refund the excess distance fare; the only row that leaves the rider carrying the whole charge is row (a), which needs a traffic-justified reroute that the rider was informed of and agreed to. The rider does not dispute the chat: the driver asked at 10:46:33 and the rider answered 'Ok can, thanks' at 10:47:03, before the point of deviation, which would satisfy POL-RD-21's agreement limb. But that acknowledgment is carried solely by EV-CHAT-06012, which is impaired at weight 0.9 on SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH, so POL-GEN-02(2) caps any finding that turns on it at 0.9, while the driver's profile carries fraud_flags of 2, which under POL-GEN-22 lifts the confidence required for an AI ruling to 0.95. A row (a) NO_ACTION that leaves the rider paying the excess cannot be entered at the confidence the policy demands, and the case must be resolved on a row that does not depend on the impaired chat.

If the Judge is not persuaded that the advisory fails the intersection limb, but is also unable to find from the record that it meets it, then the traffic-justification fact POL-RD-23 needs cannot be established on this evidence, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation with the open question stated rather than an outcome inferred from the gap. POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-03 carry ESCALATE for this category, and on an escalation no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than collected, so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge.

The deviation is established as 1.40 km, and it is over the tolerance: POL-RD-22 measures deviation as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km, the platform's recorded distances, and this record carries 17.60 km actual against 16.20 km recommended. That is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, which puts the case in the 'over 1 km' limb of the POL-RD-24 matrix. The trip record is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance (POL-RD-22).

POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of a deviation by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. The chat shows exactly that: the driver wrote at 10:46:33 'Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?' - a brief reason, which the clause says is enough - and the rider answered at 10:47:03 'Ok can, thanks'. DISCLOSURE under POL-GEN-02(1): the chat artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.9; the issue code that fired is SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH (severity LOW), a version tag on an export that is not truncated and whose four messages map one-to-one, and it does not touch the acknowledgement recorded.

The notice came before the point of deviation, not after it. The trip record's own event log places route_deviation_detected at 10:49:23 at the CTE / Yio Chu Kang Road exit, and the driver's message was sent at 10:46:33 - nearly three minutes earlier - and read by the rider at 10:47:23, before her reply. The driver's message timestamps are independently carried by the COMPLETE trip record's messages_during_trip block (MSG-06012-003 and MSG-06012-004), so this timing does not depend on the impaired chat export.

ledger.claim: The 4.80 SGD the rider claims has no basis in the policy's arithmetic. POL-RD-24 fixes the only sum the matrix can return on this record at the excess distance fare - deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge - which is 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD, and that only on rows (b) and (d), neither of which applies here. The ledger confirms per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, total_charged 21.41 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the claimed figure is overstated several times over on the rider's own best case.

The notice and the acknowledgement do not stand or fall on the impaired chat export. The COMPLETE trip record, weight 1.0, independently lists MSG-06012-003 (driver, 10:46:33) and MSG-06012-004 (rider, 10:47:03) in its messages_during_trip block, and POL-GEN-02(2) takes the highest weight among independent artifacts carrying the deciding fact. The single impairment in this record - the chat log at 0.9 for SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH - therefore does not lower the weight of the agreed-deviation finding, and I name it rather than presenting it as clean.

This is a case the AI may finish on this record. The contested amount is 4.80 SGD, and the facts that decide it - the recorded distances, the message timestamps, the advisory window and its type - all rest on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, the only impairment being a 0.9 schema tag on the chat export. Whatever elevated confidence POL-GEN-22 requires where a profile carries fraud flags is met on this record, and POL-RD-25's condition on an AI ruling is satisfied, so no escalation is called for.
